Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-1609", "title": "Fifth Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Fifth disease, also called erythema infectiosum, is a viral infection caused by parvovirus B19."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This virus only infects people; it's not the same type of parvovirus that dogs and cats can get."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It often causes a bright red rash on their cheeks (sometimes called a \"slapped cheek\" rash)."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "In the United States, parvovirus B19 infections are more common in late winter, spring, and early summer."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "There are usually minor outbreaks of fifth disease about every 3 to 4 years."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Parvovirus B19, which causes fifth disease, can spread from person to person: Through respiratory droplets, such as saliva (spit), sputum, or nasal mucus."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The droplets can spread when: Someone who has the virus coughs and sneezes You touch an item that has the virus on it Through blood or blood products From a pregnant parent to the baby during pregnancy You are most contagious early in your infection, when you usually only have a fever or cold-like symptoms."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You are not likely to be contagious after you get later symptoms such as a rash and joint pain."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "About 2 out of 10 people who get a B19 parvovirus infection will have no symptoms."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "But most people will get the symptoms of fifth disease, which are usually mild and can include: Fever Headache Cough Sore throat Rashes Joint pain The \"slapped cheek\" rash is more common in children."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They usually get the rash a few days after they first have other symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The rash can then spread to the arms, legs, chest, back, and buttocks."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Adults who get fifth disease might also have joint pain and swelling (called polyarthropathy syndrome)."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Sometimes the infection can cause serious health complications affecting the nerves, joints, or blood system."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This is more likely to happen if you are pregnant, have a blood disorder such as anemia , or a weakened immune system ."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Because of these risks to you and some possible risks to your baby, contact your health care provider if you are pregnant and: You show signs of fifth disease (or a \"slapped cheek\" rash) You may have been exposed to someone who has the infection How is fifth disease diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "There is no routine lab test to diagnose fifth disease."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Providers can often diagnose fifth disease just by seeing the \"slapped cheek\" rash and rashes on the body."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "There is testing to show whether or not you have protection (immunity) against the B19 parvovirus or if you have had a recent infection."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "This test is usually not needed, but your provider may order the test if you are pregnant or at higher risk for complications of the disease."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What are the treatments for fifth disease?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There is no specific treatment for fifth disease."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "It is usually mild and goes away on its own."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Taking acetaminophen can help with the fever and pain."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Do not give aspirin to children, because it may cause Reye syndrome ."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "This is a rare, serious illness that can affect the brain and liver."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There is no vaccine to prevent fifth disease."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "But you can help protect yourself and others by: Washing your hands often with soap and water Covering your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze Avoiding touching your eyes, nose, and mouth with unwashed hands Avoiding close contact with people who are sick Staying home when you are sick Most people become immune to the virus after having it once."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5356", "title": "Finger Injuries and Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "You use your fingers and thumbs to do everything from grasping objects to playing musical instruments to typing."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "When there is something wrong with them, it can make life difficult."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Common problems include: Injuries that result in fractures (broken bones), ruptured ligaments and dislocations Osteoarthritis - wear-and-tear arthritis."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Tendinitis - irritation of the tendons Dupuytren's contracture - a hereditary thickening of the tough tissue that lies just below the skin of your palm."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It causes the fingers to stiffen and bend."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Trigger finger - an irritation of the sheath that surrounds the flexor tendons."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It can cause the tendon to catch and release like a trigger."}]}, {"id": "MLP-34", "title": "High Blood Pressure", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Each time your heart beats, it pumps blood into the arteries."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your blood pressure is highest when your heart beats, pumping the blood."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "When your heart is at rest, between beats, your blood pressure falls."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Your blood pressure reading uses these two numbers."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Usually the systolic number comes before or above the diastolic number."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "For example, 120/80 means a systolic of 120 and a diastolic of 80."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "High blood pressure usually has no symptoms."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "So the only way to find out if you have it is to get regular blood pressure checks from your health care provider."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Your provider will use a gauge, a stethoscope or electronic sensor, and a blood pressure cuff."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They will take two or more readings at separate appointments before making a diagnosis."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Blood Pressure Category Systolic Blood Pressure Diastolic Blood Pressure Normal Less than 120 and Less than 80 Elevated 120 - 129 and Less than 80 High Blood Pressure Stage 1 130 - 139 or 80 - 89 High Blood Pressure Stage 2 140 or higher or 90 or higher Hypertensive Crisis (dangerously high blood pressure - seek medical care right away) Higher than 180 and Higher than 120 For children and teens, the health care provider compares the blood pressure reading to what is normal for other kids who are the same age, height, and sex."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "What are the different types of high blood pressure?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "There are two main types of high blood pressure: Primary, or essential, high blood pressure."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This is the most common type of high blood pressure."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "For most people who get this kind of blood pressure, it develops over time as you get older."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "This is caused by another medical condition or use of certain medicines."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It usually gets better after you treat that condition or stop taking the medicines that are causing it."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Why do I need to worry about high blood pressure?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "When your blood pressure stays high over time, it causes the heart to pump harder and work overtime, possibly leading to serious health problems such as heart attack , stroke , heart failure , and kidney failure ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What are the treatments for high blood pressure?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Treatments for high blood pressure include heart-healthy lifestyle changes and medicines ."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You will work with your provider to come up with a treatment plan."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "It may include only the lifestyle changes."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "These changes, such as heart-healthy eating and exercise, can be very effective."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But sometimes the changes do not control or lower your high blood pressure."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There are different types of blood pressure medicines."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Some people need to take more than one type."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If your high blood pressure is caused by another medical condition or medicine, treating that condition or stopping the medicine may lower your blood pressure."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-324", "title": "Meningitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Meningitis is inflammation of the thin tissue that surrounds the brain and spinal cord, called the meninges."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You get it when a virus enters the body through the nose or mouth and travels to the brain."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Bacterial meningitis is rare but can be deadly."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It usually starts with bacteria that cause a cold-like infection."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It can cause stroke , hearing loss , and brain damage."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Pneumococcal infections and meningococcal infections are the most common causes of bacterial meningitis."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Anyone can get meningitis, but it is more common in people with weak immune systems."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Meningitis can get serious very quickly."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You should get medical care right away if you have: A sudden high fever A severe headache A stiff neck Nausea or vomiting Early treatment can help prevent serious problems, including death."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Tests to diagnose meningitis include blood tests, imaging tests, and a spinal tap to test cerebrospinal fluid."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Antibiotics can treat bacterial meningitis."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Antiviral medicines may help some types of viral meningitis."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Other medicines can help treat symptoms."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "There are vaccines to prevent some of the bacterial infections that cause meningitis."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1610", "title": "Hormone Therapy for Menopause", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Menopause is the time in a woman's life when her menstrual periods stop."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "During menopause, the body makes much lower amounts of the hormones estrogen and progesterone."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Hormone therapy for menopause involves taking estrogen, with or without progesterone (or a similar hormone called progestin)."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The goal is to replace some of the hormones the body no longer makes and help relieve menopausal symptoms."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "What does hormone therapy for menopause treat?"}, {"id": "S005", "text": "In the years leading up to menopause, and during menopause, hormone levels can rise and fall."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "These changes can cause symptoms for some women that may be mild and go away on their own."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "For others, symptoms may be more severe and affect daily life."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Lower hormone levels during menopause can cause symptoms such as: Hot flashes Night sweats Mood changes Vaginal dryness Pain during sex Hormone therapy may help relieve these symptoms."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It may also help protect against osteoporosis ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Who should not use hormone therapy for menopause?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Hormone therapy is not right for everyone."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You should not use hormone therapy for menopause if you: Are pregnant or think that you may be pregnant Have unexplained vaginal bleeding Have had certain types of cancer Have had a stroke or heart attack Have had blood clots Have liver disease Talk with your health care provider about your medical history before starting hormone therapy."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "What are the types of hormone therapy for menopause?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "There are different types of hormone therapy for menopause."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "If you had surgery to remove your uterus ( hysterectomy ) your provider may recommend estrogen only therapy."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "If you still have your uterus, your provider may recommend estrogen plus progesterone (or progestin) therapy."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Hormone therapy for menopause comes in several forms."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Most are pills taken by mouth, but there are also skin patches, gels or sprays, vaginal creams, tablets, or rings."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Your provider can help you choose the type and form that's best for you."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What are the risks of hormone therapy for menopause?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "For some women, it may increase the risk of: Blood clots Heart attack Stroke Breast cancer Gallbladder disease The level of risk depends on the type of hormone therapy, how long it is used, and your medical history and lifestyle."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You and your provider should talk about the risks and benefits."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "If you decide to use hormone therapy, it is usually recommended to use the lowest dose that helps and for the shortest time needed."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Ask your provider how often you should follow up."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Many recommend checking in every three to six months at first, then once a year after treatment is working well."}]}]
